title: restore transparent substrate recovery for MCP reads
description:
The canonical DuckDB substrate has been quarantined and rebuilt repeatedly after fatal ART/index failures. The current rebuilt database contains partial source tables but zero substrate_promotion_run/evidence_graph_build rows, while the status manifest belongs to an older 10.45 GB generation and is rejected by the current-file identity check.

Unpinned MCP read routes call ensure_substrate_materialized_for_read(), but evidence_graph_substrate has no entry in _materializers(). ensure_materialized() therefore returns blocked; callers discard that result and continue, yielding apparently successful empty data. Example: lynchpin_evidence(action=timeline, 2026-07-13..14) returned ok=true/data=[] even though readiness reports no promoted snapshot.

The intended contract is transparent materialization when a requested product/window is not materialized. Recovery must preserve that contract without hiding a failed convergence result.
acceptance_criteria:
1. After a clean-schema corruption rebuild, an unpinned MCP read transparently converges the required substrate/window when local sources permit.
2. If convergence cannot run or fails, the MCP response is explicitly blocked/error; it cannot return ok=true with a vacuous empty dataset.
3. Rebuild/recovery invalidates or regenerates the status manifest and read snapshot consistently with the canonical generation.
4. A behavior test reproduces valid promotion -> corrupt rebuild -> partial source refresh -> unpinned MCP read and proves recovery or explicit failure.

title: Recover and report GitHub substrate promotion failures
description: Chisel's GitHub-context refresh can hit a DuckDB fatal checkpoint error, after which materialize_github_context swallows the failure and Chisel prints a misleading ready status. Reproduce the connection-invalidated path, retry safely with a fresh connection where possible, and surface degraded promotion status without blocking NDJSON-backed snapshot generation.
acceptance_criteria: A transient DuckDB fatal during GitHub-context promotion gets one fresh-connection retry; persistent promotion failure is represented in the returned manifest and Chisel output does not claim an unqualified ready state; focused regression tests cover both cases.
notes: Root cause evidence: the canonical DuckDB failed standalone CHECKPOINT with TransformToDeprecated, and its read snapshot passed CHECKPOINT but aborted under promotion with GetAllocatorIdx. Snapshot reuse was unsafe. Implemented atomic clean-schema rebuild before quarantine/swap, one idempotent GitHub retry, fail-closed Chisel degradation, and multiline artifact-reference guarding found during full regeneration. Live recovery rebuilt 49 tables and populated core rows; forced 64-step current-state regeneration completed 63 steps plus a successful targeted rerun of the narrative; full five-repository Chisel regeneration completed with unqualified GitHub context ready and all XML well formed. Focused tests: 14 passed. Changed-file Ruff: passed. Publication checker required by instructions was absent from this checkout and PATH; complete public diff was manually reviewed. Residual Polylogue operator-day adapter drift tracked as lynchpin-4ul.
close_reason: Recovered via clean derived-store rebuild, regenerated all outputs, and verified post-Chisel checkpoint plus focused regressions.

title: substrate_run_step has recorded zero rows ever: materialization audit trail silently dead
description: Found in 2026-08-03 whole-repo correctness audit. _record_materialization_step (lynchpin/materialization.py:858) wraps recording in try/except Exception: return, and the substrate_run_step table contains 0 rows total despite materialization runs having executed for months (verified: duckdb read-only query, count(*)=0). Every recording attempt has failed silently since the mechanism was built, so DAG runs leave no audit trail: the 55-day temporal_signals staleness found in this audit could not be diagnosed from the substrate at all. Likely cause worth verifying first: duckdb single-writer lock held by long-lived MCP server connections making connect() fail on every write attempt from the materialize path. Fix direction: (a) make the recorder log its own failure (once per run, journald) instead of pure swallow; (b) if it is the writer lock, record via an append-only JSONL next to the substrate (promoted into duckdb on the next promotion pass) instead of direct writes. Related class: sinnix-e8e capture-integrity sentinel; second instance of observability-that-cannot-fail-loudly.

title: Minute-level sleep analysis to escape the night-level power ceiling

Real candidate effects (2-FMA on sleep architecture, g=0.24-0.41) sit at or below that floor, so they show consistent direction and no significance. The per-minute bins now materialized for HR, movement, respiratory, HRV and skin temperature turn a 200-night window into ~100k minute-level observations, making within-night questions well-powered on EXISTING data with no new capture. Also: pre-specify hypotheses (the 48-test scans have nominated candidates; stop scanning them), and use matched-pair designs to control the very large between-night variance (sleep-midpoint SD 3.3h). Do not impute missing nights.

title: ActivityWatch manifest covered_dates includes phantom 2010/2017-2018 dates with zero backing events
description:
events.manifest.json's covered_dates lists 3,456 dates from 2010-01-01 through 2026-07-13, but the real event data in events.ndjson only spans 2024-02-15 to 2026-07-12 (2,440,563 events, confirmed by direct earliest/latest inspection and a grep for 2017-01-30T returning zero matches). The bogus entries: 4 placeholder-looking dates (2010-01-01 through 2010-01-04, likely an uninitialized/default date artifact) and a full false 2017-01-30 through ~2018 span with no backing events.

Root cause: manifest_windows.py's merge_manifest_covered_dates() is purely accretive -- each materialization run unions the previously-recorded covered_dates with newly observed dates but never re-validates old entries against current event data (lynchpin/ingest/manifest_windows.py:35-56). Whatever produced the bad 2010/2017 dates once (early bug, stale fixture, bad merge) has been silently re-affirmed on every regeneration since, because nothing ever checks whether an old covered date still has real events.

Impact discovered 2026-08-02: this fed a wrong 'covers 9 years of ActivityWatch data' claim into the sleep_productivity join reporting (lynchpin/ingest/sleep_productivity_materialize.py consumes the same AW data) -- the real join window is ~2.4 years, not 9. Any other consumer trusting events.manifest.json's covered_dates/first_date/last_date for AW coverage claims is getting the same wrong answer.

Fix direction: either (a) make merge_manifest_covered_dates validate old entries still have backing events before carrying them forward (expensive, requires re-scanning), or (b) regenerate events.manifest.json from scratch (non-accretive) at least once to purge the phantom entries, then decide whether accretive merging is safe to keep going forward, or (c) add a sanity check/test asserting manifest first_date matches the true earliest event in events.ndjson.
close_reason: Root cause fixed in manifest_windows.py::merge_manifest_covered_dates() (verified_bounds parameter drops carried-forward dates outside the true min/max of the row set just materialized), wired into all 8 consumers, commit bac3190. events.manifest.json regenerated clean: 2010-01-01..2026-07-13/3456 dates -> 2024-02-15..2026-07-13/880 dates, verified against raw events.ndjson directly. Same audit found and fixed 4 more corrupted manifests (activitywatch/graph, IRC, atuin, spotify/daily) plus a blocking crash-on-malformed-line bug (commit b08b893). Follow-ups tracked separately: lynchpin-ee9 (unrelated keylog placeholder bug), lynchpin-mxo (atuin torn-line data loss), lynchpin-9vx (activitywatch_derived backlog), lynchpin-4pz (pytest ordering fragility). Report corrected at /realm/data/derived/reports/sleep-pipeline-audit-2026-08-02.html.

title: materialize_activitywatch_derived accumulates the whole window in memory; footprint grows unboundedly with window length
description:
Found during the lynchpin-9vx backfill (2026-08-03). materialize_
activitywatch_derived() builds window_rows for all 8 PRODUCT_KINDS
(focus_spans, daily_activity, project_focus_days, deep_work, circadian,
loops, fragmentation, attention) for the ENTIRE requested window in
memory before writing anything, plus _merge_existing_rows reads each
existing product fully. For the 760-day backfill window the working set
is ~4-6G. Consequence observed live: launched under background.slice
(MemoryHigh=2G/MemoryMax=4G) the run entered a cgroup-reclaim livelock
(memory.current pinned at exactly 2.0G, 4.58M memory-high reclaim
events, 105GB of disk reads in 48min against 5.4GB rchar -- a refault
storm at 22% CPU, extrapolated to double-digit hours; failure mode #6
in the sinnix memory-posture inventory; oomd never fires because slice
PSI stays under threshold). Mitigated one-shot by relaunching under
build.slice (22G high), per doctrine: no permanent slice-budget change.

The structural issue is that ANY sufficiently long window outgrows ANY
fixed cap. Fix direction: chunked/incremental flush -- iterate the
window in bounded spans (e.g. quarter-year), compute + merge + append
per span, and only hold one span's rows at a time, making the memory
footprint window-length-independent. Note the merge/covered_dates logic
already supports repeated sub-window calls (that is exactly what
incremental runs are), so the simplest shape may be an internal loop
that calls the existing single-window path per chunk; the current
verified_bounds/shrink-guard semantics need re-checking under that loop
(each chunk's guard sees the previous chunk's manifest, which is fine,
but per-chunk full rewrite of all 8 product files means O(chunks *
file-size) IO -- consider whether products should be written once at
the end from a streaming accumulator instead).

sleep_productivity_materialize has a milder version of the same shape
(all nights in memory) but its row counts are small; the AW derived
products are the ones with real volume. Not urgent once the backfill
completes (routine incremental windows are days-to-weeks, far under any
cap), which is why this is a task, not a bug.
close_reason: Implemented: materialize_activitywatch_derived now iterates the window in bounded chunks (chunk_days=92 default, CLI --chunk-days) calling the existing single-window merge/guard/manifest path per chunk, making peak memory window-length-independent. Regression test proves chunked==single-pass byte-identical products and bounded per-chunk generator windows. sleep_productivity variant explicitly out of scope per bead (small rows).

title: Concurrent pre-fix materializers destroyed events.ndjson (restored from btrfs snapshot); ensure-cascade rewrites canonical AW file
description:
Incident record, 2026-08-03 ~01:30-02:45 CEST. During the lynchpin-jzb /
lynchpin-9vx work, the canonical /realm/data/captures/activitywatch/
events.ndjson (2.44M rows, 625MB) was destroyed by a cascade of concurrent
materializer runs and restored from a btrfs snapshot. Sequence:

1. A sleep_productivity_materialize run launched 01:37 (with pre-ff31829,
   non-atomic-write code) internally triggers ensure-materialization of
   the activitywatch events product per window. Those ensure cycles
   repeatedly rewrote events.ndjson via truncate-then-write.
2. Concurrent readers (an activitywatch_derived narrow run 02:24, then
   the lynchpin-9vx backfill 02:31) read the file mid-truncate, saw only
   a fragment ("skipping corrupted NDJSON line" warnings), treated the
   fragment as the complete existing row set, and -- because
   materialize_activitywatch_events keeps "existing rows outside the
   window" -- persisted shrunk versions. Observed shrinkage: 2,468,166
   rows -> 206,098 rows before intervention.
3. Both writers were killed; events.ndjson + events.manifest.json were
   restored from the last consistent btrfs snapshot pair
   (realm.20260803T010000+0200: 2,440,563 rows, manifest row_count
   matching exactly), then the clean windowed regeneration was re-run
   single-writer: final state 2,468,166 rows, manifest
   2024-02-15..2026-07-12, 879 covered dates, no phantoms. The
   events_by_day index (also rebuilt from the shrunk file at 02:41) was
   fully regenerated from the restored file (row_count matches).

FIXES LANDED (2026-08-03):
- Write side: commit ff31829 -- atomic temp-file-then-rename in all 8
  manifest_windows.py consumers; a reader now always sees a complete
  old or complete new file, severing the torn-read link.
- Persistence side: commit 860c197 -- guard_incremental_shrinkage() in
  the windowed write path of all 8 consumers refuses to persist an
  incremental result that drops >50% of the manifest's recorded
  row_count (LYNCHPIN_ALLOW_SHRINK=1 to override deliberately). Tested
  with the real incident numbers. This stops the cascade even if some
  other mechanism ever produces a truncated existing-rows read again.
- Verified events_from_activitywatch_dbs reads live + archive dbs
  (_candidate_dbs), so old windows are always rebuildable from source;
  nothing was unrecoverable even in the worst case.

REMAINING OPEN QUESTIONS (why this stays open, downgraded P2->P3 since
both mechanical safeguards are in):
1. Ensure-cascade design: should derived materializers
   (sleep_productivity, activitywatch_derived) implicitly re-materialize
   the upstream canonical AW events file at all? The implicit ensure
   turns a "compute the join" run into a canonical-file writer, and two
   of those running concurrently is an ordinary occurrence (agent +
   timer). Options: ensure=False for canonical upstreams from derived
   materializers, or a cross-process write lock per canonical product.
2. Verify no other consumer read/copied the shrunk state during the
   ~20-minute damage window (02:20-02:41) -- e.g. substrate promotion or
   MCP queries.

Restoration evidence: snapshot pair realm.20260803T010000+0200; final
verified state above; incident window bounded by snapshot
realm.20260803T013000+0200 (already-torn 562K-row state at 01:30).

title: activitywatch_derived has a ~1.7yr materialization backlog (2024-02-15..2026-03-15 never computed)
description:
Found auditing manifests for lynchpin-jzb. events.manifest.json (raw AW
events) correctly covers 2024-02-15..2026-07-12 after the lynchpin-jzb

EXECUTION LOG 2026-08-03:
- First backfill attempt (02:31, background) was killed at 02:41 while
  containing the lynchpin-9tw data-destruction cascade (it was one of
  the torn-read victims/propagators; see that bead). No derived output

- After restoring events.ndjson and regenerating the events_by_day

  script: aw_chain.sh, log: /realm/tmp/work/aw-chain-20260803.log.
  Step 1 = materialize_activitywatch_derived(2024-02-15..2026-03-16);
  step 2 (only on step-1 success) = full sleep_productivity rerun,
  ordered after the backfill because sleep_productivity reads
  daily_activity per night.
- The 2026-02-15..2026-03-16 window computed by the 02:24 test run is
  suspect (it read events.ndjson mid-churn); the relaunched backfill's
  window includes it, so it gets recomputed from clean data.

VERIFICATION WHEN THE CHAIN FINISHES: check the log's step exit codes;
graph/manifest.json should show first_date 2024-02-15, no gaps between
2024-02-15 and 2026-07-12 in covered_dates, and daily_activity.ndjson's
first row dated 2024-02-15. Then sleep/productivity.manifest.json should
show a fresh materialized_at with row_count > 0.

title: personal_daily_signals has spurious zero-value keylog rows for 2010-2012 (pre-capture dates)
description:
RESOLVED 2026-08-03. Root cause confirmed and fixed.

Root cause was in _window_personal_daily_signal_rows()
(personal_signals_materialize.py), not manifest_windows.py. Each
per-source block was gated with _overlaps() (a boolean: does the outer
requested window overlap the source's real coverage at all?) but then
called that source's per-day reader with the *raw outer window*
unclipped. A full default-window run computes the outer window as the
union of every ready source's bounds, routinely much wider than any one
source's own real coverage. keylog.daily_activity() is dense: it builds
an explicit zero-filled dict for every day in [start, end) regardless of
real data, so it silently manufactured placeholder rows for every day
in the outer window outside keylog's actual capture range.

Confirmed via lynchpin.materialization.audit_materialization(): keylog's
real bounds are 2025-10-06 to today. 23,016 of 24,136 keylog rows in
daily_signals.ndjson (95%) were zero-value placeholders dated
2010-01-04 through 2025-10-05 -- a much larger contamination than the
original bead's "2010-2012" estimate (that was just the range checked
at filing time). Likely trigger: a prior full-window run whose union
bound was itself inflated by the ActivityWatch manifest bug
(lynchpin-jzb), though the underlying gating bug exists independent of
that.

Fix (commit 5dc543f, "fix(ingest): clip per-source signal windows to
each source's real coverage"): added _clip_window(), which returns the
intersection of the outer window with a source's own real
[first_date, last_date] bounds. Every per-source block now calls its
reader with that clipped range. This is a correctness fix for all 15
sources in that function, not just keylog -- no source benefits from
being asked about a window outside its own real coverage, dense or not.

Data cleanup: removed the 23,016 contaminated keylog rows directly from
/realm/data/derived/lynchpin/personal/daily_signals.ndjson (real
google_takeout rows in the same 2010-2012 span were left untouched --
those are genuine historical data, confirmed nonzero), then regenerated
the manifest via the real materializer. Before: first_date 2010-01-04,
6037 covered dates. After: first_date 2011-01-12 (google_takeout's real
earliest date), 5661 covered dates, row_count 50850. Spot-checked
"sleep" source too -- its rows now span exactly 2017-01-28..2026-03-28,
matching its own audited bounds precisely.

Tests: new test_personal_daily_signal_rows_clip_source_window_to_real_coverage
in tests/ingest/test_personal_materializers.py reproduces the bug shape
directly (narrow real coverage inside a much wider requested window,
fake dense reader) and asserts the reader is only ever called with the
clipped range. just lint / just typecheck clean; pytest
tests/ingest/ 83 passed.

title: Sleep fusion follow-ups: boundary estimator for independent-pair nights, HR binning_data
description: Deferred from the 2026-08-02 sleep-fusion reimplementation (commits 4e45e92, f5c3012; report /realm/data/derived/reports/sleep-pipeline-audit-2026-08-02.html). (1) Optional read-side best-estimate boundary for the 135 merged nights with saa_relation=independent, using deltas + signals already on the record. (2) Consider decoding heart-rate binning_data blobs if per-minute HR curves become useful. (sinex's dependency on sleep_merged_summary.csv, originally scoped here as item 2, was factually wrong -- sinex does not read sleep_merged.jsonl at all -- and is now tracked properly as sinex-side architecture work, see sinex's own beads.)
close_reason: Item 1 shipped: sources/sleep_boundaries.py adjudicates the 135 independent-pair nights against per-minute HR (113 HR-adjudicated, 37 adjusted, median 27 min, uniform 120-min clamp; commit a2800ff). Item 2 resolved: binning_data was never an opaque blob - HR rows carry plain per-minute JSON bins, now consumed by the estimator; movement bins additionally preserved in materialization and feed sleep_stage_movement() stage-consistency checks (commit 80f7daf). Bonus: proxy score refit to Samsung's own scores, 5-fold r 0.823 / MAE 6.6 (commit 30bfcb1). Deliberately not done, measured reasons in commit 80f7daf and the audit report: HRV stage fusion (AUC 0.426 deep-vs-rem), SDB flag (minute-averaged respiration cannot see apnea-scale events), respiratory/skin-temp/HRV bin preservation (no consumer yet; raw bins exist if one appears).

title: Apply atomic writes to the remaining ~12 non-manifest_windows ingest writers
description:
Follow-up to lynchpin-mxo. atomic_write_text()/atomic_write_ndjson()
(lynchpin/ingest/_manifest.py) were wired into the 8 manifest_windows.py
consumers (the ones that repeatedly rewrite one shared canonical file per
incremental run, which is the actual torn-write risk pattern). Not yet
converted: google_takeout_materialize.py, arbtt_materialize.py,
communications_materialize.py, gmail_takeout_materialize.py,
exports_materialize.py, bookmarks_materialize.py, themotte_sync.py,
title_metadata_materialize.py, activity_content_materialize.py, and two
segment writers in webhistory.py (write_raw_batch, dedup_raw_files) --
still using direct path.open("w")/write_text(). Lower priority because
most of these write fresh, content-addressed filenames per batch rather
than repeatedly overwriting one shared file, so the concurrent-writer
torn-line risk is smaller, but not zero (a crash mid-write still leaves
a truncated file at that path). Mechanical fix: swap each to
atomic_write_ndjson/atomic_write_text from _manifest.py.

title: pytest -q (full suite) has order-dependent failures unrelated to any specific change
description:
UPDATE 2026-08-03: re-investigated. The original "407 failed" full-suite
run is NOT reproducible as a deterministic ordering bug. Bisection method:
split the full collection order into first-half/second-half, run each half
plus tests/test_materialization.py (the file with the most failures).
First half + test_materialization.py: 1244 passed clean. Second half +
test_materialization.py: failed with 425 failed / 4 errors on the first
attempt, then passed clean (561/0) on a second, identical rerun of the
exact same file set, then timed out on a third attempt, then passed clean
again on a fourth (with --tb=long, no failures).

This is flakiness, not order-dependent pollution: the same test selection
produced different pass/fail outcomes run to run. It correlates with host
CPU pressure -- a concurrent heavy job was running throughout this
investigation (lynchpin.ingest.sleep_productivity_materialize doing a
~3300-day ActivityWatch join, ~95% single-core CPU for over 30 minutes,
load average ~12, ~17Gi swap in use though /proc/pressure/memory stayed
low, avg10 ~0.18%). Some tests in the failing set likely have real
timeouts or DB-lock retry windows sensitive to scheduling delay under
that load (test_prune_commit_history.py and test_substrate_views.py both
do real DuckDB I/O).

Original title "order-dependent failures" is not accurate given this
result and is corrected here rather than propagated. Downgraded to P4:
this is very likely transient resource-contention flakiness (see
CLAUDE.md Runtime Discipline: do not turn transient live-host pressure
into a permanent code-bug narrative), not a code defect. Not closed
because it was never re-verified on a fully quiet host with zero
concurrent heavy jobs -- if it reproduces there, this is a real bug in a
specific test's timeout/retry assumptions and should be re-opened as P2
against the specific flaky test, not the whole suite. Re-run
`direnv exec . pytest -q` (whole suite, nothing else running) to check.

title: atuin history.ndjson had a torn/corrupt line (data loss, one command lost)
description:
RESOLVED 2026-08-03. Root cause identified: every manifest_windows.py
consumer rewrote its full canonical NDJSON via a direct
path.open("w")/path.write_text(), which truncates the destination before
the new content is fully written. A crash mid-write or two overlapping
runs of the same materializer can leave a torn/partial file -- exactly
what the atuin torn line looked like.

Fix (commit ff31829, "fix(ingest): write canonical NDJSON and manifest
files atomically"): added atomic_write_text()/atomic_write_ndjson() to
lynchpin/ingest/_manifest.py (temp-file-then-Path.replace(), the same
pattern already used by github_context_materialize.py and
machine_materialize.py) and wired it into all 8 manifest_windows.py
consumers' writers plus write_manifest() itself. New regression test
(tests/ingest/test_manifest.py) simulates a mid-write crash and asserts
the destination file is never left truncated.

Original two follow-ups from this bead:
1. Write-path lock/atomicity fix -- DONE, see above.
2. One-time audit of other high-volume append-only ndjson sources for
   the same torn-line pattern -- scoped down to the 8 manifest_windows.py
   consumers plus write_manifest, since that's where the accretive-merge
   bug (lynchpin-jzb) already required auditing real data anyway.
   Remaining ~12 non-manifest_windows ingest writers tracked separately
   as lynchpin-7bs (lower priority: they write fresh, content-addressed
   filenames per batch, not one repeatedly-rewritten shared file).

The one truncated atuin command entry itself remains unrecoverable and
was dropped (documented in the original description).
